# The explicit surface of SELECT queries this package may run against
# events or match_summary — RFC-001 §7.1's "nothing reads them as
# authority" (issue #321). An allow-list, not a deny-list, the same shape
# and reasoning as scripts/bots-isolation-allowlist.txt: read by
# projections_test.go's TestProjectionReadsAreAllowlisted, which enumerates
# every -- name: query in internal/store/queries/*.sql whose SQL body's
# leading statement is a genuine SELECT against events or match_summary — an
# INSERT ... RETURNING (UpsertMatchSummary) is a write, not a read, and is
# not in scope here — and fails the build if one isn't listed below with a
# stated caller, or if an entry here names a query that no longer exists.
#
# One bare query name per line — the name after "-- name: ", not qualified.
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.
#
# M3's own queries here are InsertEventsBatch, DeleteEventsByMatch,
# UpsertMatchSummary and DeleteMatchSummaryByMatch — none of them a read.
# This list is empty today: cmd/replay --rebuild (M4) is the first
# regenerator of these tables, not a reader of them, and no lobby/recap read
# path exists yet. When M4/M5 add one, its query name goes here, next to a
# comment naming the caller and why reading a derived, rebuildable
# projection is safe for that specific use — see the header above for what
# "safe" has to mean: never treated as authority over the order log.
